{{nihongo|'''Kawara Shrine'''|川原神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

[[ja:川原神社 (伊勢市)]]

{{wikidata link|Q17209206|ja|川原神社 (伊勢市)|check_date=2026-05-17}}

==Old translation==

'''Kawara Shrine''' (川原神社, *Kawara Jinja*) is an auxiliary shrine (*sessha*) of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine) of the [[Ise Grand Shrine]], located in [[Ise]], {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}, Japan.

== Overview ==
Ranked 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the {{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|皇大神宮|zh|皇大神宮}} (Inner Shrine)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>.

This shrine was established by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}}, with its enshrined deity considered the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|en|Miya River (Mie)|qid=Q6884164|lt=Miya River's}} [[Chinjugami|guardian spirit]]<ref name="ic3">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.70</ref><ref name="gk2">Gakken Publishing (2013): p.71</ref>.

It is located on the eastern bank of the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk2" />, at 1559 Izumi, Sochi-cho, Ise City, Mie Prefecture<ref name="tm2">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p.76</ref>. The place name "Sochi" means "marshland," indicating the presence of marshes from the Miyagawa River<ref name="gk2" />. Records also mention rice offerings to the Inner Shrine from Sochi<ref name="sk62">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.346</ref>.

The shrine is referred to as "Kawahara Shrine" in the ''Kōtai Jingū Gishiki-chō'' and also appears as "Kawara Shrine" or "Kawara-sha" in other records. Locally, it has been called "Senzui" (川水, meaning river water or spring), "Odago," and "Yagura"<ref name="sk52">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.345</ref>.

== Grounds ==
The shrine precinct covers an area of 3,219 m²<ref name="sk72">Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): p.347</ref>. The grounds are serene, with sunlight filtering through trees, accompanied by the sounds of birds and flowing water<ref name="ic3" />. The forest includes species such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|en|Chamaecyparis obtusa|qid=Q917187|lt=Chamaecyparis obtusa}}, {{ill|Camphora officinarum|en|Camphora officinarum|qid=Q158722|lt=Camphor tree}}, {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|ja|カシ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oak|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q796117}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|en|Machilus thunbergii|qid=Q5792073|lt=Machilus thunbergii}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|en|Ilex latifolia|qid=Q2706373|lt=Ilex latifolia}}<ref name="sk72" />.

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is '''Mikoto no Mitama of Tsukuyomi''' (月読尊御魂)<ref name="ic3" />. This deity is also worshipped at the {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|ja|月夜見宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi-no-Miya1=Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto}}, part of the 125 shrines of the Ise Grand Shrine<ref name="tm2" />. Although commonly regarded as a moon deity, the connection between the moon and water is emphasized here, with Tsukuyomi revered as a river deity at Kawahara Shrine<ref name="ic3" />.

Some theories suggest that both Sochi-cho, where Kawahara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-cho, home to Tsukuyomi-no-Miya, share historical ties through the {{ill|Arakida clan|ja|荒木田氏}}<ref name="sk62" />.

== History ==
According to legend, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|en|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|qid=Q4388732|lt=Yamatohime-no-mikoto}} was greeted here by Ōwakako no Mikoto (大若子命) before sailing down the Miyagawa River<ref name="ic3" />. The shrine was established before the compilation of the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|zh|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}'' in 927 CE, which defines the auxiliary shrines of Ise<ref name="ic22">Ise Bunka-sha (2008): p.22</ref>. According to the ''Daijingū-shiki'', it was one of the shrines maintained by the Guji (宮司), receiving imperial offerings during the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}} and {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}<ref name="sk52" />.

However, during the {{ill|Sengoku Period (Japan)|ja|戦国時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sengoku period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q117415390}}, ritual practices ceased, and the shrine fell into disrepair<ref name="tm2" />. The hereditary priests (祝部) also disappeared<ref name="sk62" />.

In 1663 (Kanbun 3), {{ill|Kawabe Masanaga|ja|河邊精長}} restored the shrine in Sochi<ref name="sk52" />. A new shrine building was erected on October 9, 1663, and the deity was ceremonially transferred (遷御) on January 10, 1664<ref name="sk52" />. Descendants of former priests were sought to resume their duties<ref name="sk62" />. While local traditions guided the shrine's restoration, some suggest that the original site may have been {{ill|Takegahana Shrine|ja|竹鼻神社}} in Takegahana-cho or {{ill|Kawarabuchi Shrine|ja|河原淵神社}} in Funae<ref name="tm2" />.

Since the deity's transfer in 1694 (Genroku 7), the shrine has remained in its current location<ref name="sk52" />. The shrine was rebuilt in 1908 (Meiji 41)<ref>Ujiyamada City Hall (1929): p.11</ref>, renovated in 1960 (Shōwa 35), and repaired again in 1983 (Shōwa 58)<ref name="sk62" />.

== Rituals ==
During the {{ill|Kinensai|en|Kinen-sai|qid=Q118906710|lt=Kinen-sai}}, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|en|Kannamesai Festival|qid=Q11255045|lt=Kannamesai}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518|lt=Niiname-sai}}, and other special ceremonies, priests offer sacred food (御饌) and ritual offerings (幣帛) at the shrine<ref name="sk62" />. For ceremonies like the {{ill|Saitan-sai|ja|歳旦祭}}, remote rituals are conducted at the {{ill|Gojōden|ja|五丈殿}} of the Inner Shrine<ref name="sk62" />.

== Access ==
The shrine is located within a grove just off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|ja|三重県道22号伊勢南島線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefectural Route 22|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11357908}}<ref>Shikinaisha Kenkyūkai (1990): pp.346–347</ref>.

* **By Bus:** Approximately a 12-minute walk (700 m) from the {{ill|Mie Kotsu|en|Mie Kotsu|qid=Q6843516|lt=Mie Kōtsū}} "Sochi" bus stop<ref name="ic3" />. From the bus stop, enter the alley opposite {{ill|Q11379036|ja|伊勢市立佐八小学校|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Municipal Sochi Elementary School|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11379036}}, then follow the path along the rice fields to reach the shrine<ref name="ic3" />.
* **By Train:** About 5.5 km from {{ill|Iseshi Station|en|Iseshi Station|qid=Q6079748|lt=Ise-shi Station}}, served by both {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|en|Central Japan Railway Company|qid=Q513679|lt=JR Central}} {{ill|Sangū Line|en|Sangū Line|qid=Q872023|lt=Sangū Line}} and {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|af|Kintetsu|ar|كينتيتسو|arz|كينتيتسو|az|Kintetsu Railway|da|Kintetsu Railway|de|Kintetsu|eo|Kintetsu|es|Kintetsu|eu|Kintetsu|fa|راه‌آهن کینتتسو|fi|Kintetsu-rautatiet|fj|Kintetsu|fr|Kintetsu Corporation|fy|Kintetsu Railway|ha|Kintetsu Corporation|hu|Kintetsu Railway|is|Kintetsu Railway|it|Ferrovie Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|jv|Kintetsu|ko|긴키 닛폰 철도|mr|किन्तेत्सु रेल्वे|nds|Kintetsu Railway|nl|Kintetsu|nn|Kintetsu Railway|no|Kintetsu Railway|oc|Kintetsu Railway|pl|Kintetsu|ps|کینکی نیپون ریل پټلۍ|pt|Kintetsu Corporation|ro|Kintetsu Railway|sa|किन्तेत्सु|su|Kintetsu|sv|Kintetsu Railway|th|รถไฟคินเท็ตสึ|ti|ኪንተትሱ|tr|Kintetsu Railway|ts|Kintetsu|wuu|近畿日本铁道|zh|近畿日本鐵道|zh_classical|近畿日本鐵道|zh_yue|近畿日本鐵道|qid=Q1531085|lt=Kintetsu}} {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|en|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|qid=Q900630|lt=Yamada Line}}<ref name="sk52" />.

'''Kawara Shrine''' (かわらじんじゃ) is an {{ill|Setsumatsusha|Q1071160|qid=Q1071160|lt=sessha}} of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168}}{{ill|Kōtai Jingū|Q11581011|qid=Q11581011}} (Inner Shrine).

=== Overview ===
It ranks 20th among the 27 auxiliary shrines of the Inner Shrine.<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): pp. 9–11</ref>

It is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} designated by {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}}, and the {{ill|Saijin|Q11591100|qid=Q11591100}} is said to be the {{ill|Guardian deities|ja|守護神|qid=Q131278957}} of the {{ill|Miya River (Mie)|Q6884164|qid=Q6884164}}.<ref name="ic">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 70</ref><ref name="gk">Gakken Publishing (2013): p. 71</ref>

The shrine is located on the east bank of the Miyagawa River,<ref name="gk"/> at 1559 Sensui, aza Sōchi, Sōchi-chō, {{ill|Ise, Mie|Q328067|qid=Q328067}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Mie|af|Mie-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Mie|ar|ميه (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Mie|az|Mie prefekturası|azb|میه اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Mié|be|Міэ|bg|Мие|bn|মিয়ে প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Mie|cdo|Mie-gâing|ce|Ми (префектура)|ceb|Mie-ken|ckb|پارێزگای میێ|cs|Prefektura Mie|cy|Mie (talaith)|da|Mie-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Mie|eo|Gubernio Mie|es|Prefectura de Mie|et|Mie prefektuur|eu|Mie (prefektura)|fa|استان میه|fi|Mien prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Mie|frr|Mie (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Mie|gl|Prefectura de Mie|hak|Mie-yen|he|מיאה (מחוז)|hi|मिऐ प्रीफेक्चर|hr|Mie (prefektura)|hu|Mie prefektúra|hy|Միե (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Mie|ilo|Prepektura ti Mie|it|Prefettura di Mie|ja|三重県|ka|მიეს პრეფექტურა|km|មីអិ(ខេត្ត)|ko|미에현|la|Mieensis|lt|Mijės prefektūra|lv|Mie prefektūra|mk|Мие (префектура)|mn|Миэ муж|mni|ꯃꯤꯏ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|मिई प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Mie|ne|मिए|nl|Mie (prefectuur)|no|Mie (prefektur)|nov|Mie Prefekture|os|Миэ|pam|Prepektura ning Mie|pl|Prefektura Mie|pnb|ضلع مائی|pt|Mie|ro|Prefectura Mie|ru|Миэ|se|Mie prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Mie|si|මියේ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Mie Prefecture|sk|Mie (prefektúra)|sr|Префектура Мије|su|Préféktur Mie|sv|Mie prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Mie|tg|Префектураи Мие|th|จังหวัดมิเอะ|tl|Prepektura ng Mie|tr|Mie|tt|Ми (префектура)|uk|Префектура Міє|ur|میہ پریفیکچر|vi|Mie|war|Mie (prefektura)|wuu|三重县|zh|三重县|zh_classical|三重縣|zh_min_nan|Mie-koān|zh_yue|三重縣|qid=Q128196}}.<ref name="tm">Tatsumi Publishing (2013): p. 76</ref> The place name “Sōchi” means “marshland,” indicating that wetlands from the Miyagawa once existed there.<ref name="gk"/> There are also records stating that rice was offered from Sōchi to the Inner Shrine.<ref name="sk6">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 346</ref>

The shrine name appears as “Kawara Shrine” in the *Kōtaijingū Gishikichō*, while other sources list it as “Kawara Shrine” or “Kawara-sha.” Records state that local residents referred to it as “Senzui” (river water, spring water), “Odago,” or “Yagura.”<ref name="sk5">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 345</ref>

=== Precincts ===
The shrine grounds cover an {{ill|Area|Q11500|qid=Q11500}} of 3,219 {{ill|Square metre|Q25343|qid=Q25343|lt=m<sup>2</sup>}}.<ref name="sk7">Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): p. 347</ref> The {{ill|keidai|Q11429002|qid=Q11429002}} form a tranquil space filled with dappled sunlight, birdsong, and the murmur of the river.<ref name="ic"/> Trees such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|Q917187|qid=Q917187}}, {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}}, {{ill|Cyclobalanopsis|Q796117|qid=Q796117}}, {{ill|Machilus thunbergii|Q5792073|qid=Q5792073}}, and {{ill|Ilex latifolia|Q2706373|qid=Q2706373}} grow densely within the grounds.<ref name="sk7"/>

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|lt=Tsukuyomi|Q595520|qid=Q595520|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama}}.<ref name="ic"/> This is the same {{ill|Kami|Q524158|qid=Q524158|lt=kami}} worshipped at the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsukiyomi-no-miya}} and {{ill|Tsukiyomi-no-Miya (Gekū)|Q11516023|qid=Q11516023}}, among the 125 shrines of Ise Grand Shrine.<ref name="tm"/> While Tsukuyomi is generally regarded as a {{ill|Moon|Q405|qid=Q405}} deity, the moon and {{ill|Water|Q283|qid=Q283}} are considered closely related, and in the context of Kawara Shrine, Tsukuyomi no Mikoto no Mitama is regarded as a river deity.<ref name="ic"/>

In addition to sharing the same enshrined deity, there is a theory that Sōchi-chō, where Kawara Shrine is located, and Nakamura-chō, where Tsukiyomi Shrine is located, were both deeply connected through the {{ill|Arakida clan|Q11618716|qid=Q11618716}}.<ref name="sk6"/>

=== History ===
According to tradition, {{ill|Yamatohime-no-mikoto|Q4388732|qid=Q4388732}} was welcomed here by Ōwakako-no-Mikoto and traveled down the Miyagawa River by boat.<ref name="ic"/> Regarding its establishment, based on the definition of auxiliary shrines of Ise Grand Shrine, it is believed to have been founded before the compilation of the *{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}*, that is, before the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|de|Enchō|fa|انچو|fr|Ère Enchō|ia|Encho|id|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|ko|엔초|ru|Энтё|simple|Enchō|sr|Енчо|tr|Enchō|uk|Ентьо|zh|延長 (日本)|zh_yue|延長 (年號)|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}).<ref name="ic2">Ise Bunka-sha, ed. (2008): p. 22</ref> According to the *Daijingū-shiki*, it was designated as one of the shrines involved in repairs by the {{ill|Gūji|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500}}, and it received offerings during the Kinensai and Kannamesai festivals.<ref name="sk5"/> However, during the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}, {{ill|Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824}} were discontinued,<ref name="tm"/> and the shrine grounds fell into ruin.<ref name="sk5"/> The hereditary priests ({{ill|Gūji|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500|lt=hafuri}}) who had been appointed until then also died out.<ref name="sk6"/>

In the 3rd year of {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} ({{ill|1663|Q7577|qid=Q7577}}), {{ill|Kiyonaga Kawabe|Q92924151|qid=Q92924151|lt=Kawabe Kiyonaga}} restored the shrine at Sōchi.<ref name="sk5"/> On the 9th day of the 9th month (lunar calendar; {{ill|Gregorian calendar|Q12138|qid=Q12138}}: {{ill|October 9|ab|Жьҭаарамза 9|af|9 Oktober|als|9. The shrine buildings were rebuilt in November {{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 41).<ref>Ujiyamada City Office, ed. (1929): p. 11</ref> They were subsequently rebuilt again in May {{ill|1960|Q3754|qid=Q3754}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 35), and repairs were carried out in September {{ill|1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434}} (Shōwa 58).<ref name="sk6"/>

=== Rituals ===
During the Kinensai, {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|ja|月次祭|simple|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11516161}} (June and December), {{ill|Kannamesai Festival|Q11255045|qid=Q11255045}}, {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|de|Niiname-sai|fr|Niiname-no-Matsuri|id|Niiname-no-Matsuri|ja|新嘗祭|ko|신상제 (11월)|simple|Niiname-no-Matsuri|qid=Q11501518}}, and extraordinary festivals, {{ill|Kannushi|Q60523|qid=Q60523}} present {{ill|Shinsen|Q11591045|qid=Q11591045|lt=shinsen}} and {{ill|Hanpei|Q11481885|qid=Q11481885}} before the shrine. For rites such as the {{ill|Saitan-sai|Q11546824|qid=Q11546824}}, remote worship is performed at the Inner Shrine’s Gojōden Hall.<ref name="sk6"/>

=== Access ===
The shrine is situated in a forest slightly off {{ill|Mie Prefectural Road Route 22|Q11357908|qid=Q11357908}}.<ref>Shikinaisha Research Association, ed. (1990): pp. 346–347</ref>

* About a 12-minute walk (700 {{ill|Metre|Q11573|qid=Q11573|lt=m}}) from the “Sōchi” {{ill|Bus stop|Q953806|qid=Q953806}} on a {{ill|Mie Kotsu|Q6843516|qid=Q6843516}} {{ill|Transit bus|Q1373492|qid=Q1373492}}.<ref name="ic"/> Enter the alley opposite {{ill|Ise Municipal Sōchi Elementary School|Q11379036|qid=Q11379036}} near the bus stop and follow the rice paddies to reach the precincts.<ref name="ic"/>
* Approximately 5.5 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224|lt=km}} from {{ill|Iseshi Station|Q6079748|qid=Q6079748}} on the {{ill|Sangū Line|Q872023|qid=Q872023}} of {{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679}} or the {{ill|Yamada Line (Kintetsu)|Q900630|qid=Q900630}} of {{ill|Kintetsu Railway|af|Kintetsu|ar|كينتيتسو|arz|كينتيتسو|az|Kintetsu Railway|da|Kintetsu Railway|de|Kintetsu|eo|Kintetsu|es|Kintetsu|eu|Kintetsu|fa|راه‌آهن کینتتسو|fi|Kintetsu-rautatiet|fj|Kintetsu|fr|Kintetsu Corporation|fy|Kintetsu Railway|ha|Kintetsu Corporation|hu|Kintetsu Railway|is|Kintetsu Railway|it|Ferrovie Kintetsu|ja|近畿日本鉄道|jv|Kintetsu|ko|긴키 닛폰 철도|mr|किन्तेत्सु रेल्वे|nds|Kintetsu Railway|nl|Kintetsu|nn|Kintetsu Railway|no|Kintetsu Railway|oc|Kintetsu Railway|pl|Kintetsu|ps|کینکی نیپون ریل پټلۍ|pt|Kintetsu Corporation|ro|Kintetsu Railway|sa|किन्तेत्सु|su|Kintetsu|sv|Kintetsu Railway|th|รถไฟคินเท็ตสึ|ti|ኪንተትሱ|tr|Kintetsu Railway|ts|Kintetsu|wuu|近畿日本铁道|zh|近畿日本鐵道|zh_classical|近畿日本鐵道|zh_yue|近畿日本鐵道|qid=Q1531085}}.<ref name="sk5"/>
